title: CLAIM: A CIA program literally named 'Operation Mockingbird' ran the U.S. press
summary: The NAME 'Operation Mockingbird' first appears in Deborah Davis's 1979 Katharine Graham biography and appears in NO released CIA or congressional document. Three real things get conflated: Frank Wisner's 'Mighty Wurlitzer' foreign propaganda network; the ~50 domestic journalist relationships documented by the Church Committee; and the real 'Project Mockingbird' — a narrow 1963 warrantless wiretap of two columnists (acknowledged in the CIA 'Family Jewels,' 2007).
tldr: The Senate's Church Committee page documents the 1975–76 investigation of U.S. intelligence abuses — but the page never mentions 'Mockingbird' at all.
ai_summary:
AI review of the Senate's Church Committee overview page, read in full:
- Establishes: select committee created January 1975 (Senate resolution approved 82–4), chaired by Senator Frank Church, final report issued April 29, 1976; ~800 witnesses interviewed, ~110,000 documents reviewed.
- Its work led to the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence (1976) and the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (1978); the page names exposed programs including NSA's SHAMROCK and MINARET and the FBI's COINTELPRO.
- The page contains NO mention of 'Operation Mockingbird,' Deborah Davis, the 'Mighty Wurlitzer,' the ~50 journalist relationships, or the 1963 'Project Mockingbird' wiretap.
- Discrepancy flag: the record summary's specific claims — that the name 'Operation Mockingbird' first appears in Davis's 1979 book, appears in no released CIA or congressional document, and that three real things get conflated — could not be verified from this source; none of those facts appear on the page reviewed. Verification against the named primary source is therefore incomplete.
